sections.heading: 2. Build a permissioned evidence pipeline, not a scraping project
paragraphs: Start with a Python standard-library collector, SQLite, and a shared document store whose access is limited to the pod. Use urllib.request only for documented, permitted interfaces; use csv for authorized exports, json for responses, hashlib for document fingerprints, and zoneinfo for time handling. Manual entry is an acceptable adapter when a marketplace supplies no supported feed. Separate source records, lots, assets, inspections, quotes, bids, acquisitions, sales, and cash events. A lot can contain multiple assets, and the same asset can appear in a relisted lot. Build source keys from platform, seller, and lot identifier; build physical identities from verified VINs or manufacturer and serial combinations. Never merge two machines merely because their model names match. Store observed_at, source_updated_at when provided, retrieval method, document location, and content digest. Preserve closing and removal timestamps in UTC together with the original timezone and source wording. For date-only removal terms, retain date precision rather than fabricating a midnight deadline. Operator B owns import exceptions and identity merges; operator A resolves physical ambiguity with the seller. This division gives each discrepancy an accountable owner without requiring another full-time analyst or a custom software team before the first purchase.

Make retrieval behavior conservative and observable. Set connection timeouts, bound response sizes, validate content types, and reject unexpected redirects to credential collection pages. Use conditional requests with ETag or Last-Modified only where supported. Honor Retry-After, apply exponential backoff with jitter, and stop a failing adapter after a bounded retry budget. Keep credentials outside saved responses and versioned files; redact tokens from logs. A successful HTTP response is not proof of a successful import: a login page can arrive with status 200. Check required fields, pagination completion, duplicate identifiers, currency, timezone, and plausible item counts. Quarantine changed schemas instead of silently dropping inconvenient fields. Use sqlite3 integrity checks and foreign keys, transactionally commit complete imports, and test restoration from a dated backup. Build a small fixture collection from permitted, sanitized examples and run unittest against parsers before changing adapters. The first dashboard should show stale shortlisted lots, missing removal deadlines, unresolved identity conflicts, overdue invoices, and inventory without a buyer channel. It should not reward the team for collecting thousands of listings that nobody can inspect or remove. An outage should trigger a manual shortlist review, not unauthorized collection through a different endpoint or account.

Use the waterfall to protect the scarce resource: inspection and decision time. P1 requires VIN resolution before a paid history report. P2 requires attachment verification before freight pricing. P3 requires a recoverable component count before catalog enrichment. P4 requires a mechanic's bounded repair estimate before optimistic resale comparisons. P5 requires disposition permission before assigning parts value. P6 requires buyer specifications and credible demand before travel. Route only shortlisted assets into paid services, and record which answer justified the expense. Build a weekly exception meeting around purchases delayed by data gaps, not a tour of every dashboard chart. The mechanic receives photographs and fault questions in one packet; the carrier receives dimensions, weights, loading conditions, and the removal window; the bookkeeping contractor receives reconciled invoices, fees, and asset allocations. Contractors should receive only the records needed for their assignments. Operator B measures research minutes per purchased asset, duplicate-alert rate, stale-record rate, and the share of inspections that change a bid. Cancel a data subscription when its evidence duplicates an existing source without improving decisions. Keep a manual export and source-contact route for every critical adapter so a vendor outage cannot erase the pod's ability to operate during an auction week.

sections.heading: 3. Turn title, DEMIL, recall, and transport evidence into purchase controls
paragraphs: Treat SF-97 as evidence used in a state titling process, not as a universal substitute for a state title. Confirm what the selling agency will issue, whether the purchaser name must match the account, which original documents accompany delivery, and what the destination motor vehicle agency requires. A release document proves permission to collect property; it does not necessarily prove a complete ownership chain. Under 41 CFR Part 102-38, federal personal-property sales operate within a defined sales framework, but the actual solicitation and award terms still determine inspection, payment, and removal obligations. State registration, resale permitting, tax, and dealer requirements depend on location and transaction pattern. The Driver's Privacy Protection Act, 18 U.S.C. § 2721, limits disclosure and use of personal information from motor vehicle records; use authorized record-access procedures rather than searching for prior owners through unrelated personal-data services. Where security interests matter, investigate the relevant debtor, collateral, jurisdiction, and release documents. UCC search results require interpretation, especially for certificate-of-title property. Do not infer clean ownership from a government-looking seller name or a single database result. Operator A must connect the physical asset to the exact documents that support the planned resale channel.

Keep military disposition, export classification, and product safety as separate questions. A DEMIL code addresses a particular disposition framework; it does not automatically answer whether a component may be exported, sold to a particular buyer, or marketed for civilian use. Review DLA instructions, the selling activity's conditions, technical identifiers, and any mutilation or destruction requirements before assigning parts value. The Export Administration Regulations in 15 CFR Parts 730–774 can apply to equipment and components, while defense articles may fall under a different export regime. Route ambiguous military-origin material to qualified classification review rather than inventing a favorable classification. For consumer products within CPSC jurisdiction, 15 U.S.C. § 2068 prohibits specified sales involving recalled and otherwise noncompliant products. Match the actual model and affected serial range; a similar photograph is insufficient. Vehicle recalls require their own NHTSA and manufacturer workflow, and a public search cannot prove every repair was performed. P5 should never become a mechanism for stripping identifiers or separating parts to avoid a restriction. Retain disposition evidence for every restricted lot, and keep potentially affected goods physically separated from ordinary inventory until the desk establishes a permissible handling and sale path.

Removal feasibility deserves the same evidence standard as title. An attractive hammer price can become a loss when a machine cannot be started, tires cannot hold pressure, a forklift lacks capacity, or an agency allows collection only during a narrow appointment. Translate seller terms into a carrier packet with dimensions, weight source, lifting points, loading assistance, site restrictions, appointment contacts, and the final removal date. Verify carrier identity with FMCSA records where applicable, then obtain cargo coverage and equipment suitability evidence separately. A USDOT number alone does not establish adequate coverage or available capacity. Build a pre-bid exception checklist covering as-is defects, document delivery, restricted-item conditions, buyer fit, and deadline risk. Assign each unresolved item an owner and a decision date earlier than auction close. Operator A can reject a purchase; operator B can withhold a ready-for-sale status when documentation or inventory reconciliation is incomplete. Neither should silently convert a missing fact into a favorable assumption. Preserve the rejected packet as well as the purchased packet: repeated rejection reasons reveal which agencies, asset classes, and removal sites consume effort without producing usable inventory. That feedback improves sourcing more reliably than simply increasing alert volume.

sections.heading: 4. Make every information expense reconcile to owner profit
paragraphs: Keep the canonical scorecard visible beside the operating dashboard. Conservative revenue is $150,000 of gross resale proceeds at an 8% net margin, producing $12,000 annual owner net profit with two full-time staff and three contractors. Base revenue is $575,000 at 14.0%, producing $80,500 with the same staffing configuration. Scaled revenue is $1,000,000 at 20%, producing $200,000 with three full-time staff and four contractors. These figures describe the resale business, not the total auction value observed, seller transaction volume, or value of unsold stock. The corresponding total cost envelopes are $138,000, $494,500, and $800,000. Acquisition, buyer charges, transport, refurbishment, paid data, software, storage, selling expenses, and other operating costs must fit inside those envelopes under the scorecard's accounting convention. Do not add subscription spending beneath owner profit as though it were free. The stated $15,000–$80,000 startup capital range and $3,000–$15,000 monthly operating-expense range describe planning boundaries, not permission to combine every high-cost assumption with the Conservative case. Reconcile a specific budget before purchasing inventory. Track inventory acquisition as a cash requirement and recognize the relevant cost against sales consistently; cash deployment and period expense are related but different measures.

Use a transparent bid worksheet instead of a model that turns weak comparisons into false precision. For an illustrative asset expected to resell for $10,000, reserve $1,400 for owner profit and $2,200 for all non-acquisition costs, including allocated overhead. Assume a 10% buyer premium on hammer price and no additional acquisition tax in this particular example because the transaction's documented tax treatment supports that assumption. The hammer ceiling is ($10,000 minus $1,400 minus $2,200) divided by 1.10, or $5,818.18. Hammer plus premium therefore consumes approximately $6,400, total costs equal $8,600, and the resulting $1,400 profit matches a 14% margin. This is a teaching example, not evidence that every asset achieves Base economics. Replace the tax assumption and premium formula with the actual sale terms. Round down to an allowed bidding increment, and treat the ceiling as a stop price rather than a target. If inspection raises repair costs by $660, the hammer ceiling falls by $600 under the same premium structure. If buyer demand weakens, change expected proceeds first; do not preserve the bid by quietly deleting the profit reserve or ignoring storage.

Evaluate tooling through attributable changes in decisions and cash conversion. A proposed $200 monthly data service costs $2,400 annually, equal to 20% of Conservative owner profit and approximately 3% of Base owner profit before any benefit. Its justification must come from measured avoided losses, lower research labor, better realized proceeds, or faster turnover that fits the pod's actual capacity. Record the baseline, the decision changed, the evidence used, and the realized outcome; do not count a hypothetical avoided purchase as a booked gain. Review purchased assets by play, seller, age, repair variance, transport variance, and realized margin. Separate asking-price comparisons from completed transactions and net offers. Unsold inventory needs a dated repricing or liquidation decision, not a dashboard valuation that grows with optimism. Operator B closes the weekly exception report; operator A resolves bid and removal issues; contractors supply bounded technical, transport, and bookkeeping inputs. Add the third full-time role and fourth contractor only within the Scaled plan's seven-person structure and cost envelope. Automation should increase the number of fully evidenced decisions the existing pod can execute, not multiply weak leads, overdue collections, or assets stranded at a government yard.

chapters.title: Contracts, Statutory Guardrails, Licensing & Outreach Scripts
chapters.subtitle: GSA Sale Terms, SF-97 Title Chains, DEMIL Restrictions, State Dealer Boundaries, and B2B Resale Contracts
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #17, Government Surplus Auctions, ranks #29 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score because paperwork, removal capacity, and inventory risk constrain otherwise attractive spreads. This chapter organizes six mapped plays: fleet vehicles, material-handling equipment, shop machinery, office technology, commercial furnishings, and industrial spares. Each requires a documented eligibility decision, enforceable purchase terms, a resale pathway, and a buyer-specific outreach script. Conservative, Base, and Scaled annual owner profits are $12,000, $80,500, and $200,000 on $150,000, $575,000, and $1,000,000 gross resale proceeds. The operating system assigns contracts and bid control to two full-time operators, supported by three contractors, while separating federal sale conditions from state licensing, title, tax, and restricted-property requirements.

sections.heading: 1. Classify the seller, the sale authority, and the six resale pathways
paragraphs: Start every acquisition by identifying the legal seller, the platform operator, and the authority governing disposal; those are three separate fields in the bid file. Federal personal-property sales generally sit within 40 U.S.C. § 545 and 41 CFR part 102-38, while donation authority under 40 U.S.C. § 549 creates a different eligibility and use regime. A public bidder must not treat a donation program as ordinary resale inventory. GSA Auctions listings, GovPlanet contractor sales, and municipal listings on GovDeals or Public Surplus can impose materially different payment, inspection, and removal obligations. Platform branding alone does not establish ownership, federal status, or the right to receive a vehicle title. Save the complete listing, incorporated conditions, amendments, photographs, and seller answers before bidding; preserve the final version after award. The full-time acquisition lead records which document controls if terms conflict and sends unresolved conflicts to the named seller contact. The second full-time operator checks resale feasibility and cash exposure independently. Neither an auction alert nor a completed bid-limit worksheet substitutes for eligibility review. Require the account holder, paying entity, invoiced purchaser, and intended title applicant to align unless the seller expressly permits another arrangement.

Use six mapped plays as the chapter's operating taxonomy: fleet vehicles, material-handling equipment, shop machinery, office technology, commercial furnishings, and industrial spares. Fleet vehicles require a VIN-level title pathway, odometer treatment, and a dealer-license determination before any resale promise. Material-handling equipment requires serial verification, battery or fuel-system condition, and a loading plan that matches actual weight. Shop machinery adds guarding, rigging, disconnect responsibilities, and meaningful inspection access. Office technology requires ownership evidence, lawful software treatment, and documented data sanitization before resale. Commercial furnishings turn on access, building protection, packaging, and freight economics rather than headline unit counts. Industrial spares require part-number verification, traceability, and a restricted-property screen; ambiguous military markings are a stop signal, not a marketing advantage. These plays share one five-person pod, not six parallel businesses. Contractor one handles licensed transport or rigging within their credentials, contractor two performs category-specific inspection or refurbishment, and contractor three supplies transaction administration and qualified specialist coordination. Replace or supplement contractors when credentials do not match the lot. The acquisition lead owns restrictions and bid ceilings; the resale lead owns buyer qualification, inventory records, and collections.

Separate disposal eligibility from permission to export, demilitarize, operate, or resell. A government auction award does not waive the Export Administration Regulations in 15 CFR parts 730-774, state hazardous-material rules, or the conditions attached to controlled property. For a GovPlanet or other defense-related lot, capture the actual DEMIL designation, purchaser certifications, end-use restrictions, required forms, and release conditions supplied for that lot. Do not infer that a civilian-looking asset is unrestricted, or that a platform's screening answers every downstream export question. An End-Use Certificate, when required, concerns the specified transaction; it is not a transferable export license. Keep restricted components outside the ordinary office, machinery, and spares sales pipeline until a qualified reviewer resolves their classification. For municipal assets, check the selling agency's disposal authority and listing conditions rather than importing federal procedures automatically. Public records exposure also varies: mark genuinely sensitive material specifically, but do not promise customers that an agency will keep every commercial communication private. Under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(4), federal protection for qualifying confidential commercial information is contextual, and state disclosure statutes differ. Budget review time before bidding, because a removal clock rarely pauses for the buyer's research.

callout.title: Buy the documentary pathway before buying the asset
callout.body: Experienced surplus operators price missing evidence as a real execution cost and reject defects that money cannot cure within the removal window.
items: Ask the seller for the exact vehicle document type and named issuing entity; a photograph of an example SF-97 does not establish the documents promised for your VIN.
Save auction amendments immediately before bidding and again after award, because removal instructions and incorporated terms can change outside the headline description.
Ask whether loading equipment is available to purchasers, not merely present onsite; obtain written responsibility for operators, rigging, and equipment damage.
Maintain a separate restricted-property queue so an ordinary industrial-spares listing cannot bypass review through an automated inventory import.

sections.heading: 2. Resolve state licensing, tax, title, and sector boundaries before bidding
paragraphs: Build a state-by-state transaction card around the business location, storage yard, purchase state, delivery state, and buyer type. Dealer licensing is not a universal annual vehicle-count rule. California Vehicle Code § 11700 establishes licensing requirements for persons acting as vehicle dealers, subject to the applicable definitions and exceptions; Texas Transportation Code § 503.021 addresses the general distinguishing number requirement. Wholesale activity, brokering, salvage vehicles, and conducting business from a yard can create separate obligations. Do not assume that selling only to businesses removes them. Before entering the fleet play, send the relevant licensing authority a factual description of ownership, advertising, sales frequency, premises, and customer types, then retain its written direction or obtain state-specific professional analysis. A resale certificate also does not replace a business license or dealer credential. California Revenue and Taxation Code § 6066 governs seller's permit applications; other states use different registration and exemption processes. Collect resale certificates appropriate to the transaction and validate their required fields. Track economic and physical nexus separately, including inventory stored by contractors. Where a marketplace collects tax, preserve its transaction report and confirm which sales remain the operator's responsibility.

Treat SF-97 as evidence supporting an application for a state certificate of title, not as the state title itself. Before bidding, confirm that the receiving motor-vehicle agency accepts the offered document package for that vehicle class and ownership chain. Record whether the seller promises SF-97, an existing title, a bill of sale, or another instrument; those documents are not interchangeable. Match VINs physically, investigate alterations, and identify liens, salvage branding, off-road limitations, and missing assignments. Federal odometer disclosure duties under 49 U.S.C. § 32705 and 49 CFR part 580 depend on the vehicle and applicable exemptions; avoid the obsolete assumption that every vehicle over ten years old is exempt. Model year, age, weight, and transaction facts matter. A buyer's willingness to accept paperwork risk does not make a defective transfer valid. For forklifts and machinery, the absence of a motor-vehicle title does not eliminate ownership diligence: examine serial records, seller authority, and any relevant security interests. Under state enactments of UCC § 2-312, warranty-of-title issues require separate treatment from condition disclaimers. Keep questionable chains out of customer listings until the resale lead can describe exactly what ownership documents will be delivered.

Sector requirements follow the asset and the work actually performed. Used electronics should leave with a serial-level sanitization record and a clear statement about included operating systems; NIST guidance can inform the process without becoming a claim of government certification. Refrigeration equipment may implicate Clean Air Act refrigerant-handling requirements, including 40 CFR part 82, subpart F, when servicing or disposal occurs. Lead-acid batteries, oils, and other materials need a transport and waste determination based on their condition and intended disposition; labeling every defective unit as reusable does not resolve hazardous-waste obligations. Workplace use of powered industrial trucks invokes employer duties under 29 CFR § 1910.178, but a seller must distinguish those duties from a representation that a used forklift is ready for every buyer's workplace. Use qualified contractors for regulated services and retain their credentials, scope, and disposal receipts. The five-person pod cannot economically become a title office, environmental service company, export specialist, and equipment inspector simultaneously. Narrow the catalog when specialist availability or documentation is weak. A $15,000-$80,000 startup capital envelope must fund deposits, freight, holding time, and repairs, not merely winning bids; unresolved licensing consumes both capital and calendar.

callout.title: Four pre-flight checks that must clear before a binding bid
callout.body: The acquisition lead records each decision; the resale lead independently checks the supporting evidence rather than accepting a verbal assurance.
items: Verify purchaser eligibility, account identity, payment entity, and any required end-use documentation against the actual seller's terms.
Verify state dealer, tax, title, and sector requirements for the intended resale route, including storage and delivery jurisdictions.
Verify that a qualified carrier can meet the removal deadline with the specified loading resources, insurance, and site access.
Verify that the bid ceiling includes every acquisition and resale cost while leaving sufficient cash for delayed release or unsold inventory.

sections.heading: 3. Contract for the actual asset, cash exposure, and five-person workload
paragraphs: Read the auction purchase contract as a cash-and-performance schedule, not merely an asset description. Capture the deposit, buyer premium, payment method, taxes, inspection rights, default remedies, pickup appointment rules, and final removal deadline. Identify when ownership and risk of loss pass; payment, release authorization, loading, and delivery may be different events. Record whether the seller supplies loading assistance, whether dismantling is permitted, and who bears damage to the premises. Federal sales are not automatically governed by every FAR clause used for government procurement: apply the actual sale authority and incorporated terms. For downstream commercial resale, state enactments of UCC §§ 2-313 and 2-316 matter because factual descriptions and express warranties can defeat careless attempts to disclaim everything. Draft a condition schedule identifying tested functions, untested functions, visible defects, missing accessories, and the inspection opportunity. An as-is purchase from government does not authorize a misleading resale advertisement. Address title separately and identify exactly which documents accompany delivery. The operator's sales order should distinguish a physical inspection from a functional acceptance test, define any rejection procedure, and set a written deadline for reporting shipping damage without pretending that mandatory statutory rights disappear.

Use a short master agreement plus an asset-specific order rather than renegotiating every routine sale. Scope identifies serial numbers, accessories, preparation, packing, delivery, installation exclusions, and title documents. The fee trigger for ordinary inventory resale is the agreed purchase-price payment schedule; any separately offered sourcing service needs its own stated deliverable and earned-fee event. Never book the customer's asset budget as sourcing revenue. A narrowly drafted anti-circumvention clause can protect documented introductions for a defined period, but should exclude preexisting relationships, independently sourced contacts, and public auction listings. It cannot bind a public agency that never agreed to it or excuse bidder collusion. Liability caps should address the parties' actual risk allocation, insurance, and enforceability under governing state law, with appropriate treatment of fraud, intentional misconduct, and obligations that cannot be limited. Dispute terms specify governing law, venue or arbitration mechanics, notice addresses, and an escalation contact. Intellectual-property and data terms distinguish owned inspection photographs and reports from seller material, licensed software, and personal information found on devices. Promise deletion or transfer only where the operator has authority and a process to deliver it. Do not promise secrecy that public-records duties can override.

Reconcile contract discipline to Candidate #17's actual economics. Conservative gross resale proceeds of $150,000 at 8% produce $12,000 annual owner net profit and leave $138,000 for the modeled cost envelope. Base proceeds of $575,000 at 14.0% produce $80,500 profit and $494,500 of costs. Scaled proceeds of $1,000,000 at 20% produce $200,000 profit and $800,000 of costs. These are gross resale proceeds, not auction marketplace volume, customer purchasing budgets, or principal handled for others. Purchase prices, premiums, transport, refurbishment, selling costs, labor, and overhead must fit inside the applicable envelope. The 2 FT + 3 C staffing designation describes the Conservative and Base pod; it does not establish that either case can fund five market-rate salaries. Price actual hours and contractor engagements before accepting the model locally. Monthly operating expense of $3,000-$15,000 is a planning range, not a second deduction after costs already included in net margin. Scaled staffing increases to 3 FT + 4 C. An illustrative $4,000 removal default would consume one-third of Conservative annual profit, demonstrating why deadline controls outrank bid speed. Set inventory aging actions before purchase and prohibit discretionary rebidding with cash reserved for committed collections.

sop_steps.action: Both full-time operators verify payment instructions and release conditions before assigning contractor work.

sections.heading: 4. Use permission-aware outreach that sells evidence rather than affiliation
paragraphs: B2B outreach is not outside communications law. Commercial email must satisfy 15 U.S.C. § 7704, including accurate transmission information, nondeceptive subjects, required identification, a valid physical postal address, and a working opt-out method. Honor opt-outs within ten business days and maintain the mechanism for the required period; the statute generally requires thirty days after transmission. Retain a minimal suppression record so a later contact import does not restart messages to someone who opted out. Use business contact information relevant to the recipient's role, and do not scrape personal mobile numbers for automated texts. Calls and texts require a separate assessment under 47 U.S.C. § 227, 47 CFR § 64.1200, and applicable state rules; the equipment, message purpose, number type, and permission history matter. Begin with individually reviewed business email and manual calls to published business lines, checking applicable calling restrictions rather than assuming manual dialing removes them. Never imply that the operator represents GSA, a municipality, or a defense agency merely because inventory originated there. Contractors must use the same suppression list and approved claims. The resale lead reviews campaign samples and records the source of each prospect contact.

Use this seller discovery script before bidding: "I am evaluating lot 184 for commercial resale. Which entity is the seller, which terms control, and what ownership documents will accompany this exact asset? Please confirm the payment deadline, final removal date, loading responsibility, and any purchaser or downstream-transfer restrictions in writing." Replace the lot number with the actual listing identifier. For a vehicle, continue: "Does this VIN receive an SF-97, an existing title, or only a bill of sale? Who issues that document, when is it available, and are any brands or use restrictions recorded?" For machinery, ask: "Which functions were tested, who disconnects the equipment, and may our insured rigger inspect the route before bidding?" For office technology, ask: "Are storage devices included, what sanitization records exist, and which software rights, if any, transfer?" These questions request facts, not preferential access or exceptions unavailable to other bidders. When the seller cannot answer, record the uncertainty and reduce the bid only if a lawful, practical resale route remains. A low price cannot repair a missing ownership chain or prohibited transfer. Put every answer into the lot file before the acquisition lead commits capital.

Use this buyer email body: "Commercial equipment offer: we independently resell used material-handling equipment acquired through public auctions. We have an inspected electric pallet truck available with serial photographs, a condition report, and delivery pricing. Does your team purchase this equipment, and who specifies capacity and battery requirements? Reply with your requirements if you would like the asset packet. To stop commercial emails from us, reply STOP." Send it only with a truthful subject, accurate sender identity, and the business's actual physical postal address in the signature. Do not claim inspection unless the record exists. On discovery, say: "What load weight, aisle width, power arrangement, delivery location, and acceptance test must this unit satisfy? We will document tested functions and defects before you decide." For a sourcing request, say: "Are you buying our inventory or asking us to locate an asset for your account? We use separate written terms so ownership, fees, and payment responsibilities stay clear." End with an evidence-based next step, not artificial scarcity: "I can send the current condition packet and a written delivered-price offer with its actual validity period." Log requirements, permission signals, objections, and opt-outs in the inventory-linked contact record.

chapters.pull_quote: The profitable bid is the one whose ownership, restrictions, removal plan, and buyer promises survive contact with the paperwork.
action_checklist: Assign every prospective lot to one of the six mapped plays and document the actual seller, sale authority, purchaser eligibility, and controlling terms.
Complete the purchase, storage, and destination state transaction card for licensing, tax, title, and sector-specific requirements before committing capital.
Obtain written ownership-document commitments, restricted-property findings, contractor credentials, and executable removal arrangements for the specific asset.
Issue an asset-specific resale order covering scope, payment, condition, title, liability, disputes, and intellectual-property or data responsibilities.
Configure auction alerts, bid-limit worksheets, inventory records, and outreach suppression controls around the two-full-time, three-contractor pod.
Reconcile gross resale proceeds and all operating costs to the $12,000, $80,500, and $200,000 annual owner-profit cases without counting customer principal as revenue.

chapters.question_prompt: How does a 2 FT + 3 C (5 people) government surplus auctions team automate 70%+ of repetitive research, qualification, fulfillment, and traffic/deal acquisition while keeping human-in-the-loop QA?

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #17, Government Surplus Auctions, ranks #29 with a Money-to-Manpower Score of 79/100: automation must reduce clerical drag without disguising capital and handling intensity. This chapter maps six operator plays: auction discovery, evidence qualification, bid-limit underwriting, removal coordination, inventory remarketing, and buyer reactivation. A 2 FT + 3 C pod uses Python collectors, structured LLM extraction, deterministic worksheets, and exception queues to target 70%+ automation of measured repetitive tasks. Humans retain bidding, condition, title, restricted-item, and release decisions. Canonical annual owner profits remain $12,000 Conservative, $80,500 Base, and $200,000 Scaled; the Scaled case requires 3 FT + 4 C. Evidence-linked listings and segmented B2B outreach create repeatable distribution without treating auction principal, unrealized inventory value, or buyer deposits as additional revenue.

sections.heading: 1. Instrument six operator plays before automating the auction inbox
paragraphs: Build the operating system around six mapped plays: auction discovery, evidence qualification, bid-limit underwriting, removal coordination, inventory remarketing, and buyer reactivation. These are this chapter's execution labels, not six separate revenue businesses. The first full-time operator owns sourcing, underwriting, and purchase authorization; the second owns inventory, sales, and collection. Assign the three contractors to inspection, transport, and refurbishment or specialist documentation, with written availability rather than assumed daily coverage. Contractors can contribute evidence but cannot silently change a bid ceiling or release an asset. Every lot receives a stable internal identifier linked to platform, seller, auction identifier, lot identifier, and original URL. GSA Auctions, GovPlanet, GovDeals, and Public Surplus differ in seller relationships, documents, fees, and pickup procedures; record the actual seller instead of inferring federal ownership from the platform name. Store source snapshots, retrieval timestamps, and document hashes alongside normalized fields. A Python sqlite3 database is sufficient for one controlled writer; use a transaction-backed shared database when multiple workers must reserve the same stock. The central design objective is one accountable asset record, not an elaborate dashboard that reproduces contradictory spreadsheets across five people's inboxes.

Acquire listings through seller-provided alerts, permitted exports, and documented interfaces where available. Do not assume these auction platforms provide public bid APIs or outgoing webhooks. A mailbox collector can use imaplib and email to ingest alerts; urllib.request can retrieve permitted resources with explicit timeouts and rate limits. Persist raw messages before parsing, then emit your own signed internal event for a newly observed or changed lot. Validate its signature, timestamp, body size, and event identifier before processing. Use hashlib.sha256 over stable source identifiers and content to separate duplicate deliveries from genuine revisions. Auction closing times need zoneinfo time zones and daylight-saving handling, not server-local arithmetic. Keep the advertised closing time separate from the latest observed extension; soft-close behavior makes an early snapshot unsuitable for final bidding. A seller's changed removal deadline should create an exception immediately, even when the title and asking price remain unchanged. If collection fails, retain the last successful snapshot, mark freshness explicitly, and send the sourcing operator a direct link for manual review. Never let a failed fetch look like an empty auction or permission to reuse stale terms.

Define the automation denominator before claiming seventy percent. Instrument repeatable digital task instances, such as deduplication, field extraction, worksheet recalculation, pickup reminders, listing draft creation, and buyer-segment assignment. In an illustrative two-week sample of 200 eligible instances, 144 completed without manual editing yields 72% straight-through task completion. Count a task requiring correction as assisted, even if software produced most of the draft. Report human-review minutes, exception frequency, and rework separately; this result does not mean seventy-two percent of total labor, inspection, loading, or judgment disappeared. Keep consequential decisions outside that denominator and report their counts visibly so the metric cannot improve through selective omission. Initially inspect every extraction, then reduce sampling only for low-risk fields after measured accuracy supports the change. Continue reviewing fees, deadlines, identifiers, restriction language, and money before commitment. The weekly pod meeting should compare automated completions with missed pickups, inventory aging, and realized contribution per lot. A system that processes more alerts while buying slower-moving equipment has accelerated the wrong activity. Pause a failing play independently rather than disabling inventory controls or buyer suppression with the entire workflow.

callout.title: Automate the paperwork that experienced surplus operators distrust
callout.body: The strongest shortcuts preserve provenance and surface exceptions before cash, trucks, or customer promises become committed.
items: Snapshot seller-specific payment and removal terms at review and again before bidding; platform branding does not standardize local pickup rules.
Request loading-door dimensions, forklift availability, dock height, and loading assistance in writing before calculating freight for oversized machinery.
Treat SF-97 availability, the actual vehicle identifier, and the destination state's title process as separate checks rather than one vehicle-document checkbox.
Record why qualified buyers reject a lot; missing voltage, dimensions, attachments, or test evidence often explains poor conversion better than price.

sections.heading: 2. Separate probabilistic extraction from deterministic bid and release controls
paragraphs: Use the LLM as a constrained evidence extractor, never as the source of auction terms. Send a bounded document excerpt and request a JSON object containing field name, extracted value, exact supporting quotation, source location, and an uncertainty flag. Python json parsing, explicit type checks, required-field validation, and allowlisted units should reject malformed output. Treat seller descriptions, PDFs, and emails as untrusted data: instructions embedded inside them must not change the extraction policy, call tools, or publish listings. Keep API credentials outside prompts, redact buyer details, and send only the material required for the task. OCR can confuse vehicle identifiers, decimal points, and equipment model suffixes, so compare critical fields against photographed plates or original documents. An absent SF-97 reference means documentary status requires review, not that a certificate will accompany the sale. SF-97 supports vehicle titling; it is not itself a state-issued title. Where a DEMIL designation or controlled item is involved, record the applicable seller conditions and verified disposition requirements. Do not translate a code into unrestricted resale eligibility from memory. Route unresolved items to the sourcing operator before any purchase or external product claim.

Calculate bid ceilings with decimal.Decimal and an explicit fee basis. For an illustrative equipment lot, assume realizable resale proceeds of $12,000, freight of $900, refurbishment of $600, selling costs of $600, a defect reserve of $800, and required contribution of $2,200 before shared overhead. This leaves $6,900 for hammer price plus buyer premium. With a 10% premium on hammer and no acquisition tax in this example, the algebraic hammer ceiling is $6,272.72 when rounded downward to cents. The executable ceiling must be the highest permitted auction increment below that amount; a $100 increment would cap the bid at $6,200. A verified tax obligation, minimum premium, payment surcharge, or different taxable base changes the formula and requires recalculation. Do not treat the $2,200 contribution target as annual owner profit or an achieved lot outcome. Attach freight quotes, comparable sales, and repair assumptions to the worksheet version. Model restricted access, missing attachments, and incomplete testing as costs or reasons to reject the lot rather than allowing optimistic language to inflate the resale estimate. The human bidder must see the current version and remaining cash exposure before acting.

Implement a durable state machine: discovered, evidence collected, qualified, bid authorized, won, removal scheduled, received, listed, reserved, sold, and released. Rejected and disputed are explicit branches, not deleted records. Each transition requires an actor, timestamp, source version, and evidence appropriate to the action. A generated email is not a sent email, a payment instruction is not cleared payment, and a pickup reservation is not physical receipt. Use an outbox table so a database commit and its pending notification remain recoverable after a process crash. Retry safe reads with capped exponential backoff; reconcile payment, reservation, and publication status before retrying actions that could duplicate commitments. For deadline-sensitive tasks, alert a named person rather than trusting endless retries. The inspector uploads condition evidence, the transport contractor confirms collection constraints, and the operations lead reconciles received quantity and serial numbers against the purchase record. Contractual removal dates remain controlling unless the seller provides a written extension. Preserve both the original deadline and authorized revision. The same discipline prevents a vehicle with unresolved title documents from being advertised as ready for immediate registration simply because a listing template inserted that phrase.

callout.body: Automation may assemble the packet, but the accountable operator records the final decision against the exact source version.
items: Verify seller identity, bidder eligibility, applicable resale documentation, and item restrictions using current terms rather than a previous auction's packet.

sections.heading: 3. Turn verified inventory into programmatic, referral, and outbound distribution
paragraphs: Start the distribution flywheel at receiving, not after a listing has failed. The inventory record should contain measured dimensions, weight basis, voltage, serial number, attachments, testing method, observed defects, title-related status, location, and loading constraints. Generate a draft asset page from those fields and attach original photographs that the business owns or is authorized to reuse. The operations lead checks every condition assertion before publication. Separate observed operation from full functional testing: a machine that powers on has not demonstrated rated output under load. Generate programmatic category pages only when they offer meaningful inventory, buying criteria, or documented sold examples; thin pages that substitute town names create maintenance work without helping industrial buyers. Mark sold assets accurately, remove purchase actions, and offer relevant available stock rather than baiting buyers with unavailable bargains. Store page version and publication identifier so a corrected voltage or defect disclosure can propagate across the website and approved marketplaces. Do not delete adverse condition evidence from the internal record when marketing copy changes. Better evidence reduces repeated questions, improves freight quoting, and gives procurement teams something concrete to circulate internally before asking for a purchase order.

Build outbound around buyer fit and available inventory, not bulk address volume. Maintain company-level segments such as municipal fleet repair shops, warehouse operators, fabrication businesses, equipment dealers, and educational laboratories. Capture category interest, service geography, voltage requirements, loading capability, and whether the buyer needs title-ready vehicles. An LLM can draft a short message from approved facts, but deterministic rules must exclude sold stock, suppressed recipients, and unsupported claims. U.S. commercial email, including business-to-business messages, must meet applicable requirements of 15 U.S.C. 7704, including accurate headers, nondeceptive subject lines, required advertising identification, a valid postal address, and a working opt-out mechanism. Honor opt-outs within the statutory period and preserve suppression across system migrations. Do not purchase scraped personal addresses or use automated outreach to conceal sender identity. Start with existing customers, inquiries, and appropriately sourced business contacts; obtain permission before publicizing customer names or purchase details. Cap outreach by the team's ability to answer technical questions and arrange inspection. Measure qualified replies, inspection bookings, paid orders, and gross resale proceeds attributable to a campaign. Open rates are unreliable operational targets, and a lead without payment is not recognized resale revenue.

The referral loop should make verification portable. After a completed sale, send the buyer a concise asset packet with operating observations, collection instructions already fulfilled, and a shareable link to related available equipment. Ask whether another location or purchasing colleague needs similar stock; request an introduction instead of uploading the buyer's address book. With permission, publish a factual case note explaining the application, preparation performed, and logistics solved. Avoid implying government endorsement merely because the asset originated in a public auction. Track introductions with opaque referral identifiers rather than personal information in URLs. Feed sold prices, elapsed days, lost-sale reasons, and repeat requests back into discovery filters and bid worksheets. If buyers repeatedly need single-phase equipment while intake keeps finding three-phase machines, adjust category qualification instead of increasing email frequency. Reserve inventory atomically when a serious buyer enters the agreed sales process, and give reservations an explicit expiry. A stock change should update the website, marketplace queue, and planned outreach before the next campaign runs. This closes the flywheel: trustworthy evidence attracts qualified demand, demand improves acquisition selection, and better selection reduces unsold stock consuming the pod's limited cash and handling capacity.

sections.heading: 4. Price automated runs, rehearse recovery, and scale within the scorecard
paragraphs: Price automation per accepted result, not merely per API request. For an illustrative extraction run, assume 6,000 input tokens at $2 per million and 1,200 output tokens at $8 per million. Model expense is $0.0216; add $0.004 for parsing and storage and $0.006 for allocated execution and messaging, producing $0.0316 per run. These are planning assumptions, not quoted vendor prices. One hundred runs therefore cost $3.16 before review. If twenty need two minutes of review each at an internal labor valuation of $30 per hour, review adds $20 and the batch costs $23.16, or $0.2316 per run. Count retries, abandoned outputs, OCR charges, and failed validations in the actual numerator. Divide by accepted results when reporting cost per usable extraction. Allocate fixed subscriptions separately rather than hiding them in negligible token expense. This example covers extraction review only; mandatory purchase and release decisions still consume time. The economic comparison is the previous manual process at equivalent quality. Saving three clerical minutes does not justify one missed removal deadline, an erroneous title claim, or a single purchase made above the defensible bid ceiling.

Keep every annual scenario tied to the canonical gross resale basis. Conservative revenue is $150,000 at an 8% net margin, yielding $12,000 annual owner net profit and $138,000 in implied total costs. Base revenue is $575,000 at 14.0%, yielding $80,500 profit and $494,500 costs. Both use 2 FT + 3 C. Scaled revenue is $1,000,000 at 20%, yielding $200,000 profit and $800,000 costs with 3 FT + 4 C. Purchase, transport, and refurbishment are already included in the margin basis; do not subtract those costs again or add auction purchase volume to resale revenue. Automation subscriptions, review labor, storage, and selling expenses must fit within the modeled cost envelope, not sit beneath it as invisible extras. These totals do not establish a specific wage schedule or prove that every listed team member receives full-year market compensation. Build the actual staffing budget before committing to hires. The $15,000–$80,000 startup capital range and $3,000–$15,000 monthly operating expense range are planning context, not additional revenue. Distinguish inventory cash purchases, recurring expenses, and owner distributions so a profitable sale does not conceal an approaching cash shortage.

Scale only after the measured workload fits the pod. Review weekly exception age, deadline breaches, stock accuracy, human minutes per qualified lot, and cash committed to unsold assets. Assign every recurring exception to one owner and one remediation date. Keep encrypted database backups, test restoration, restrict access by role, and rotate credentials when contractors leave. Rehearse a mailbox outage, malformed LLM response, duplicate webhook, database lock, and unavailable carrier before increasing auction coverage. During an outage, use a dated manual queue for deadlines and commitments, then reconcile it before resuming automated messages. Do not batch-replay purchase or release actions merely because notifications accumulated. Require a current inventory and payment check for each consequential action. The first expansion should remove the observed bottleneck: better inspection coverage, reliable transport capacity, or faster buyer response, rather than indiscriminate additional scraping. Moving into the Scaled case changes the roster to seven people; it is not evidence that the original five-person pod can absorb unlimited lots. Keep the seventy-percent target tied to repetitive digital work, and retain physical verification where defects, loading conditions, and title documents determine whether an apparent bargain becomes saleable inventory.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you structure a lean 2 FT + 3 C (5 people) -> 3 FT + 4 C (7 people) pod, enforce weekly scorecards, and build transferable books that command a premium exit multiple (or durable cash cow)?
chapters.title: Pod Architecture, Contractor KPIs & Exit Valuation
chapters.subtitle: GSA and Municipal Surplus Pods: SF-97 Evidence, DEMIL Controls, Contractor SLAs, Accrual Cohorts, and Buyer-Ready Earnings
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #17, Government Surplus Auctions, holds Rank #29 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score: capital and labor discipline determine whether the inventory becomes income. This chapter maps six operator plays: auction intelligence, bid underwriting, removal logistics, refurbishment control, B2B remarketing, and inventory-to-cash governance. The five-person pod comprises 2 FT + 3 C; the seven-person configuration adds one inventory controller and one independent inspection contractor. Canonical annual owner net profits are $12,000 Conservative, $80,500 Base, and $200,000 Scaled, against gross resale proceeds rather than auction transaction volume. Build weekly evidence-backed scorecards, cap customer and counterparty concentration at 25%, and reconcile each lot through accrual books. Transferability comes from documented access rights, clean title, assigned work product, and earnings that survive replacement of the owner.

sections.heading: 1. Assign six operator plays to five accountable people
paragraphs: Design the pod around six mapped operator plays, not six departments: auction intelligence, bid underwriting, removal logistics, refurbishment control, B2B remarketing, and inventory-to-cash governance. These labels provide the chapter's execution map for Candidate #17. In the five-person configuration, FT1 is the acquisition and commercial lead, usually the owner; FT2 is the operations and inventory lead. C1 supplies transport services, C2 supplies mechanical or equipment refurbishment, and C3 supplies photography, specifications, and listing production. FT1 owns auction intelligence, bid underwriting, and remarketing pricing; FT2 owns removal, refurbishment acceptance, and inventory-to-cash records. Contractors execute defined deliverables without inheriting discretionary bidding authority or unrestricted banking access. Every lot receives one identifier before bidding, one accountable employee, and one evidence folder linking the auction listing to the resale invoice. Use GSA Auctions for federal opportunities and GovDeals or Public Surplus for municipal opportunities; evaluate GovPlanet listings according to their actual seller and contractual conditions. A marketplace name never establishes the property's legal status, inspection rights, or removal obligations. This allocation preserves five actual people while separating decisions from specialist execution and keeping the owner from becoming the undocumented dispatcher for every purchase.

At the seven-person configuration, retain those five seats and add FT3 as inventory controller and sales coordinator, plus C4 as an independent inspection specialist. FT3 takes ledger preparation, buyer follow-up, receivables tracking, and document completeness from FT2; FT2 retains physical custody and release authority. C4 performs risk-selected prebid inspections and independent acceptance checks on expensive repairs. The same person should not diagnose a defect, authorize their own expanded repair scope, and certify satisfactory completion. FT1 approves bid ceilings; FT2 verifies transport and removal feasibility; FT3, when present, verifies available cash against outstanding commitments. Where the smaller pod combines recordkeeping and custody, FT1 performs a documented weekly sample count and bank reconciliation review as a compensating control. Use individual Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace accounts and role-based QuickBooks Online or Xero access; preserve exports outside the auction platform. Do not create shared marketplace credentials merely to simplify staffing. Confirm delegated account rights with each platform and agency. Add the two seats only when documented workload and realized contribution support their cost, not because a revenue target has been crossed. Scheduled capacity reviews must distinguish hours spent moving assets from hours spent correcting incomplete purchase files.

The canonical staffing counts describe operating seats; they do not establish payroll rates, contractor hours, or owner compensation. Conservative revenue of $150,000 at 8% produces $12,000 annual owner net profit; Base revenue of $575,000 at 14.0% produces $80,500; Scaled revenue of $1,000,000 at 20% produces $200,000. Corresponding total expense envelopes are $138,000, $494,500, and $800,000, including purchases, transport, refurbishment, and other costs. Never add contractor charges outside those envelopes while repeating the same profit figures. Two market-paid employees plus specialist vendors may overwhelm the Conservative envelope, particularly where acquisition costs consume most proceeds. Document whether owners occupy FT seats, what compensation is already expensed, and how much work each contractor actually performs. Build a monthly labor-capacity schedule and a separate replacement-cost schedule rather than quietly treating unpaid owner effort as transferable earnings. The stated $3,000-$15,000 monthly operating expense range represents alternative operating conditions, not an amount automatically added to every scenario. Likewise, $15,000-$80,000 of startup capital must cover inventory funding and timing gaps without being mistaken for revenue. If actual costs exceed a canonical envelope, report the variance and redesign workload, purchasing, or pricing before claiming that scenario is executable.

callout.title: Build the institutional memory before the second warehouse
callout.body: Surplus operators lose margin in undocumented exceptions. Capture these four artifacts while the people who handled the lot can still explain them.
items: Save the auction description, amendments, photographs, and removal terms before bidding; seller pages can change or disappear after the sale.
Have C1 photograph loading access and equipment clearances before mobilizing a specialty trailer; a low hammer price cannot absorb repeated failed pickups.
Keep the SF-97 chain and state title correspondence in the same lot folder, but track them as separate documents with separate completion criteria.
Record actual teardown findings against the original bid worksheet so the next buyer of similar surplus equipment inherits defect history rather than optimism.

sections.heading: 2. Pay contractors for accepted outputs and enforce weekly evidence
paragraphs: Write a separate statement of work for each contractor lane, with deliverables, acceptance evidence, exclusions, response targets, and payment timing. For C1, an illustrative work order pays $650 for an agreed local collection and delivery, with preauthorized accessorial charges and signed custody receipts; actual quotes depend on weight, distance, permits, and equipment. For C2, use approved labor hours at a quoted rate plus documented parts, with a written stop-work threshold before teardown expands the job. For C3, an illustrative $125 accepted listing packet includes serial photographs, measured dimensions, tested functions, and disclosed defects; it does not purchase an unsupported claim that equipment is operational. For C4, quote inspection scope separately from repair work to preserve independence. Pay undisputed accepted work promptly under the agreement; define correction rights rather than inventing penalties after delivery. Do not pay a percentage of auction hammer value, which rewards larger purchases instead of profitable outcomes. Contractor status depends on the actual relationship, not the invoice label. Review federal and applicable state worker-classification requirements before imposing employee-like schedules, exclusivity, or continuous supervision on a purported independent business. Set service outcomes and safety requirements while allowing genuine vendors to control their lawful execution methods.

Run a forty-five-minute weekly scorecard meeting from a frozen Friday export, with FT1 accountable for decisions and FT2 accountable for evidence. Track bid discipline as purchases within authorized ceilings divided by all purchases; target 100%. Track timely removal as lots collected within contractual deadlines divided by lots due that week; target 100%, and escalate any threatened miss before the deadline. Track first-pass acceptance as deliverables accepted without rework divided by completed deliverables, with a starting management target of at least 95%. Track listing latency from physical receipt and completion of required tests, while separately exposing days blocked by missing documents. Report cash conversion through inventory days, receivable days, and payable days rather than celebrating booked sales while cash remains trapped. Present realized lot contribution after direct selling and handling costs alongside inventory age and warranty or return experience. Each red metric gets one owner, one dated corrective action, and one next-week verification artifact. Keep denominator counts visible: one missed removal out of two is operationally different from one out of fifty, even though both require action. Compare cohort medians and worst cases so a single successful fleet disposal cannot conceal repeated small-lot execution failures.

Enforce a maximum 25% concentration for each customer and material counterparty, using defined denominators rather than an ambiguous portfolio percentage. Aggregate related buyer entities and measure their trailing-twelve-month gross resale revenue, current receivables, and committed but uncollected orders separately. Measure each selling agency or related seller group against acquisition spend; measure transport and repair providers against their respective service-category spend and booked near-term capacity. An auction platform is a channel, not automatically the economic seller, so maintain a separate platform-dependence metric. At Base revenue, the customer revenue ceiling is $143,750; at Scaled revenue, it is $250,000. Use a 20% warning threshold to redirect prospecting, auction sourcing, and vendor qualification before the hard limit is reached. A new business with one completed sale cannot honestly claim diversified trailing revenue. Mark that startup concentration as an unresolved exception, avoid expanding the dominant exposure, and build independent counterparties before describing the portfolio as transferable. Document pre-transaction concentration projections and decline incremental exposure that would breach an established cap. Backup vendors need current quotes and demonstrated capability, not merely names in a spreadsheet. Correlated dependencies, such as two haulers sharing the same specialty trailer, count as one practical failure point during removal planning.

sop_steps.title: Freeze the operating evidence
sop_steps.action: Export the lot ledger, accounting reports, contractor work orders, and open removal commitments every Friday.
sop_steps.detail: FT2 prepares the five-person pod packet; FT3 prepares it after expansion. Preserve the reporting timestamp and identify unposted invoices.

sop_steps.title: Reconcile metrics to source records
sop_steps.action: Trace every missed deadline, rejected deliverable, concentration warning, and aged lot to its underlying transaction.
sop_steps.detail: Keep numerator and denominator counts, distinguish physical defects from document blockers, and assign correction responsibility without rewriting history.

sop_steps.title: Authorize bounded corrective work
sop_steps.action: Assign one owner, spending limit, due date, and acceptance artifact to each corrective action.
sop_steps.detail: FT1 approves commercial exceptions; FT2 controls physical execution. Contractors receive written scope changes before incurring additional charges.

sop_steps.title: Close actions against observed outcomes
sop_steps.action: At the next meeting, verify delivery, accepted repairs, corrected records, or reduced exposure before closing an action.
sop_steps.detail: Carry unresolved items forward with their original age and quantify any cash, margin, or removal consequence.

sections.heading: 3. Build accrual lot books and a transferable evidence chain
paragraphs: Build accrual books around the asset, not around the bank feed. Capitalize acquisition price, buyer premium, inbound transport, and directly attributable refurbishment where appropriate under the adopted inventory policy; apply that policy consistently with the accountant's reporting framework. Expense selling activity and general overhead according to their nature rather than hiding them in inventory to protect current earnings. Recognize gross resale proceeds when the applicable revenue-recognition conditions are satisfied, with the related carrying cost released to cost of goods sold. A customer deposit before fulfillment ordinarily remains a liability, and sales tax collected for a taxing authority is not operator revenue. For a principal reseller, the canonical $575,000 Base figure is gross resale revenue, not merchant transaction volume or a commission basis. Illustratively, a lot purchased for $6,000 with a $600 premium, $900 inbound freight, and $500 qualifying repair cost carries $8,000 before sale. A $10,000 sale creates $2,000 gross profit; $400 of selling and outbound costs leaves $1,600 contribution before overhead. That lot example does not replace the canonical 14.0% Base net margin. Show both views so operational contribution cannot be mistaken for annual owner net profit, and reconcile cash receipts separately from recognized revenue.

Close monthly by acquisition cohort, asset class, seller, and disposal channel. Preserve original purchase dates when stock moves between yards or listings; relisting must never reset aging. Reconcile physical serial numbers to the inventory subledger, the subledger to the general ledger, and sale invoices to receivables and collections. Allocate mixed-lot costs using a documented, reasonable method applied consistently, such as supported relative resale values at acquisition. Do not assign every dollar to the first item sold and present the remainder as free stock. At thirty, sixty, and ninety days, review price, market demand, missing documentation, and probable recovery costs; these are management review intervals, not universal statutory deadlines. Record write-downs when required by the reporting framework and retain support for estimated realizable values. Run the saleability review before placing replacement orders, because a profitable income statement can coexist with deteriorating inventory quality. Separate restricted cash, unpaid auction purchases, removal commitments, customer deposits, and tax liabilities in the thirteen-week cash forecast. A buyer should be able to reproduce the monthly close without asking the founder which forklift was swapped, which invoice contains freight, or why an apparently sold asset remains in the yard.

Transferable books include rights and restrictions, not just ledger balances. Federal personal-property sales under 41 CFR Part 102-38 operate within applicable agency procedures and sale terms; municipal auctions require their own seller-specific review. An SF-97 supports the government vehicle ownership chain but does not itself establish state registration, roadworthiness, or completion of every state title requirement. For defense-origin property, preserve the stated demilitarization designation, end-use conditions, and required release evidence; resolve restrictions with the seller before bidding, modification, export, or resale. Do not infer unrestricted status from a commercial marketplace listing. Review UCC title and warranty provisions as adopted in the governing state, including California Commercial Code sections 2312 and 2316 where applicable; an as-is description does not automatically erase title obligations. Obtain signed copyright assignments for contractor-created photographs, listing copy, and custom operating materials under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a), with preexisting material identified and appropriately licensed. Do not assume payment creates ownership or that every commissioned work qualifies as work made for hire. Finally, inventory platform account permissions, software licenses, customer contract assignment clauses, and lawful data-transfer conditions. A business sale cannot transfer rights that the operator never possessed.

sections.heading: 4. Price replacement-adjusted earnings before choosing an exit
paragraphs: Treat valuation multiples as negotiated hypotheses, not automatic rewards for clean folders. For a small owner-operated surplus reseller, a preliminary screening range of 1.5-3.0 times normalized seller's discretionary earnings can be useful; this is an illustrative underwriting range, not a claim about verified transaction comparables. Seller's discretionary earnings typically restores one working owner's compensation and qualifying discretionary or nonrecurring expenses to the chosen earnings starting point. Define that bridge explicitly and avoid restoring costs that a buyer must continue paying. The canonical owner net profits of $12,000, $80,500, and $200,000 are neither automatically discretionary earnings nor automatically EBITDA. Obtain the underlying expense detail before selecting either measure. At the smallest case, required inventory and equipment may dominate recoverable value, and a goodwill multiple can be economically irrelevant. At Base, owner dependence, concentrated buyers, weak title files, and slow stock can push a deal toward asset recovery rather than an earnings valuation. At Scaled, seven people still do not create institutional management automatically. Buyers pay more credibly for repeatable earnings when the operations lead can run removal, repair, and collections without the founder's personal intervention, and when evidence survives independent sampling across multiple acquisition cohorts.

Build a replacement-adjusted bridge before discussing a premium. An illustrative Base bridge starts at $80,500 canonical owner net profit, restores $12,000 of documented genuinely nonrecurring cost, deducts $65,000 of incremental replacement labor only if that labor is absent from recorded expenses, and deducts an $8,000 normalized inventory-loss adjustment. The resulting $19,500 is replacement-adjusted operating earnings under those assumptions, not EBITDA unless the remaining interest, tax, depreciation, and amortization treatment also supports that label. It is not the original scorecard profit and must never silently replace it. If owner compensation is already expensed, calculate only the documented difference between existing and replacement cost; subtracting a full salary again would double count. An illustrative 2.0-3.0 multiple on this replacement-adjusted measure produces $39,000-$58,500 of earnings-based operating value, subject to the agreed asset perimeter and working-capital terms. This is a different buyer lens from owner-operator discretionary earnings and uses a separately negotiated multiple. It shows why attractive owner income can coexist with modest transferable value. Validate all assumptions against payroll, contractor invoices, inventory loss history, and the actual duties a buyer must replace.

Negotiate the transaction perimeter before arguing over the headline multiple. Specify whether ordinary saleable inventory is included through a working-capital target or purchased separately at an agreed value; never capitalize the same stock through both mechanisms. Exclude obsolete or restricted inventory unless its recovery and obligations are explicitly priced. Reconcile enterprise value to equity proceeds through the agreed treatment of cash, debt, debt-like liabilities, working-capital adjustments, transaction expenses, and any deferred consideration. A seller note or earnout is future exposure, not cash received at closing. Build a buyer room with monthly accrual statements, cohort margins, title exceptions, contractor agreements, signed IP assignments, concentration reports, and twelve months of scorecards where operating history permits. Test transferability through a documented two-week owner absence with bounded delegated authority, then measure exceptions and lost throughput. Compare a sale with continued ownership using replacement-adjusted cash generation after maintenance spending, working-capital requirements, and reserves. The durable cash-cow choice requires the same discipline as an exit: enforce purchase limits, liquidate stale stock, maintain independent counterparties, and pay for competent execution. Retaining ownership is rational only when the resulting return justifies the capital exposure and the owner's remaining workload.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #17, Government Surplus Auctions, ranks #29 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score: this is high-leverage, system-disciplined asset trading, not passive auction arbitrage. This chapter maps six execution plays: GSA light fleet, GSA shop equipment, GovPlanet unrestricted rolling stock, GovDeals municipal equipment, PublicSurplus facilities assets, and B2B mixed-lot breakup. A two-employee, three-contractor pod spends its first month proving eligibility, bid discipline, removal capacity, and buyer liquidity before expanding inventory. Canonical annual owner profits are $12,000 Conservative, $80,500 Base, and $200,000 Scaled. Daily deliverables and Day 30/60/90 thresholds distinguish a correctable execution defect from a broken buying thesis. A first deal can take one to six months; an empty warehouse alone does not justify killing the business.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1-7: Define Six Plays, Assign Five People, and Fence the Cash
paragraphs: Start Day 1 by separating an auction account from a repeatable buying business. This chapter uses six execution labels rather than asserting six independently scored candidates: P1 is GSA light fleet; P2 is GSA shop equipment; P3 is GovPlanet unrestricted rolling stock; P4 is GovDeals municipal equipment; P5 is PublicSurplus facilities assets; P6 is mixed-lot breakup for identified B2B buyers. Assign each opportunity one primary play; a mixed lot assigned P6 cannot also inflate another play's pipeline. These are sourcing and resale lanes, not representations that every listed asset belongs to a government seller. Verify the seller and sale authority on each listing. FT1 owns sourcing, buyer interviews, bidding, and collections. FT2 owns inspection coordination, inventory custody, removal, and disposition. C1 supplies mechanical or equipment inspection, C2 supplies insured transport and loading, and C3 handles title administration and bookkeeping. Contractors receive bounded work orders rather than permanent availability assumptions. On Day 2, select two active plays using local buyer density and transport radius; retain the other four as monitored lanes. Five people cannot simultaneously inspect six asset classes, repair purchases, and run outbound sales.

Use a $75,000 opening-cash illustration within the canonical $15,000-$80,000 startup range, not a new earnings forecast. Cap operating cash burn at $9,000 per month, inside the stated $3,000-$15,000 range, and cap total pilot inventory commitments at $15,000. No individual lot may consume more than $7,500 of fully loaded acquisition cash. Maintain $25,000 of unrestricted cash after unpaid commitments; tax collections and buyer deposits reserved for refunds are unavailable for bidding. The $9,000 ceiling must cover actual recurring payroll, employer charges, insurance, storage, software, and administration. Price inspection, transport, and repair work into lot costs where directly attributable; never count the same expenditure again in overhead. If lawful staffing and quoted services exceed the ceiling, revise funded capital and the operating plan before purchasing rather than hiding unpaid labor. With $15,000 deployed and no collections, cash falls to $51,000, $42,000, and $33,000 after months one, two, and three. Another $9,000 month would breach the floor. Day 3 therefore produces a thirteen-week cash schedule showing payment deadlines, removal charges, payroll dates, and a stop-buy trigger before new obligations create a predictable shortfall.

Days 4-7 establish the evidence system. Create seller-authorized alerts on GSA Auctions, GovPlanet, GovDeals, and PublicSurplus, using saved searches rather than unauthorized collection methods. Record twenty qualified listings across the two active plays; qualification requires seller identity, removal location, sale terms, asset identifiers, and a plausible buyer segment. FT1 conducts ten buyer conversations and obtains at least six written price indications across the shortlist. Ask about configuration, pickup location, payment timing, and rejection conditions, not merely whether someone likes cheap equipment. On Day 5, C3 checks auction eligibility, resale registration, and destination title requirements. Federal personal-property sales operate under 40 U.S.C. 545 and 41 CFR Part 102-38; municipal sales require their own seller-specific authority and terms. An SF-97 supports a vehicle title application but is not itself a state title or permission to drive. On Day 6, obtain loading and transport quotes; on Day 7, reconcile the cash ledger and rank the shortlist. Export restrictions and DEMIL conditions are lot-specific: a commercial auction interface does not establish unrestricted transferability. Exclude unresolved restricted-property questions from the first pilot.
